title: Ancient Trees in Belgium: Cities to Explore
meta_description: Belgium names a national champion for each species, and one small Antwerp park holds two of them. Four cities mapped, 50 trees.
intro: Belgium keeps a national champion for each species, and one small Antwerp park hemmed in by three streets holds two of them: the thickest black locust recorded in the country at 4.10 metres, and a black mulberry at 1.28 metres, which is what a record looks like for a tree that never grows stout. Brussels runs an inventory of its own, and the first entry in it was a squat evergreen oak in the Parc d'Egmont that most people walk straight past. Six of the trees mapped here stand in that one park, within a couple of minutes of each other. The largest tree in Brussels by girth is not European at all: a giant sequoia in the Parc de Woluwe, measured at 8.66 metres around in 2017. Two cities so far, 50 trees.
